The meeting was chaired by Omar Rivera.

Omar Rivera, Theo Silva, and Minnie attended, along with the senior coordinator, the route lead, and the customer support team.

The review opened with a blunt safety check. The desk reported a few recent cases where passengers arrived with incomplete carrier details and weak pre-departure preparation, and that is not acceptable. The group agreed that clear guidance must go out earlier, in plain language, and that every traveler should be told what to expect before they reach the gate. I pressed for firmer checks on paperwork, carrier condition, and animal comfort, because rushed handling creates avoidable risk.

The route lead said the team has been fielding more pet travel questions from connecting passengers, and that replies must stay calm, accurate, and fast. A concern was raised about mixed messages between desk staff and cabin staff, so the group decided that one version of the guidance will be used for all passenger contact. The senior coordinator reminded everyone that respectful communication matters even when travelers are stressed, and the desk must avoid guesswork.

Minnie was mentioned during the discussion as a reminder that stressed animals show warning signs early, and those signs must not be ignored. <<FACT F050>> Staff noted that pet handoff checks need to be consistent and documented. <<FACT F042>> There was also a request to tighten cabin monitoring and to flag any unusual noise, odor, or distress at once. The room agreed that no one should treat a small concern as harmless when an animal is involved.

We also reviewed deck placement for larger carriers and the need to keep aisles clear. <<FACT F045>> The discussion closed with a demand for better follow-up after every trip, especially when passengers are first-time pet travelers. The team accepted that prompt reporting, careful listening, and quick correction are now urgent priorities for Aurelia Skyways.

The meeting ended in a focused and orderly manner.
